lines: You will want the small door. It sticks.
I knew you would come home eventually.
Sacks in the far bay. Mind the step.
That is all you want to say to me?
There is a supper in the barn shortly.
Rodents in the seed store. Eight.
Kill them and keep the tails.
Not the midden. The west field.
Two spits down, and cover them well.
Because we have always used the field.
Two hundred years of them under there.
Best soil in the valley, and no wonder.
Above the ford. The stretch nobody works.
Because it is ours, and we say so.
Eight, and not a small one among them.
Do not tell Whitewall what comes out
of that water. They would want a share.
Sell first. Then we chalk the post.
Their number, their number, then ours.
Why do we keep both their prices?
So ours can sit between them.
A number in the middle is never asked
about. That is the whole of the trick.
One more. The west field post.
It is in the ground already.
Two paces west of where it was.
We shift it a little most years.
Nobody has ever mentioned the field
getting bigger, and nobody ever will.
Flour off the west field. Bake with it.
Then eat it, and pay attention.
One loaf, and the work came easier.
Not like that, it does not.
Not today. Ask me in the spring.
The whole village eats in the barn once
a year. This year you cook it.
Sit at the end table. Go on.
I know you would. Sit anyway.
You will want to remember sitting there.
What if they see each other?
Then they both go home in a temper
And the hens want doing after.
Because the hens always want doing.
I am told your flour is the best here.
I am not told which field it is off.
It is a field. There are several.
Quite. I never write the field down.
Ossa. Blackstone. I will not keep you.
Weight, price, and a cart. In that order.
There is another buyer in the yard.
Then I will stand here and watch hens.
Both paid. Neither one the wiser.
That is how a village stays a village.
Pear onto thorn. Cut clean, bind hard.
The thorn does not know it is a pear.
It feeds what it is holding regardless.
Now the same thing, on your own face.
We can. Ash in the cloth. Hold still.
Three counts, and do not breathe out.
There. Say something in his voice.
The Watch reads faces, not clothes.
Remember that and you will be fine.
There has always been a cousin
in Whitewall that nobody can place.
Dob was him for eleven years.
Now it is you. His name is Ansel.
Ansel. You still owe me a drink.
I owe half the yard a drink.
You do. Where were you at harvest?
Then Ansel had a harvest. Good.
He is not a lie. He is a post,
and the house keeps somebody in it.
Eels at first light, both towns by noon.
Your own. A cart out of here is a cart.
Two towns and nobody asked me anything.
They never do. We feed them.
A face is for watching with.
The covenant is read at High.
Stand in white and count it yourself.
That is the whole of it, and it is enough.
As it is given, so it is given back.
Good. You have a Sanctum voice.
Eleven measures. I counted four times.
Eleven. Same as my grandfather had.
Then the ledger was never the lie.
No. The number they read out was.
It has been wrong since before the wall.
Three crates over. Take four off.
There will only be three on board.
There is always one already aboard.
Four off, three on. It never holds.
It has not held in forty years.
Because you load it that way.
Because we load it that way.
One crate a crossing. Nobody misses one.
The wagon goes up the Drove Road
on the eighth, and it goes covered.
Four of ours go on it at the barn.
You will want to be up there when it goes.
Sacking, then sacks. Have a look.
Half of this came out of our barn.
A bit over half, most eighth days.
They are not lying. They just never
asked whose barn it stood in first.
An eastern face wants eastern ash.
Burn them down in your own hearth.
Hold it. Do not talk yet.
Her jaw sits further forward than that.
How do you know her jaw?
I fostered her out. Same as you.
Sela. They had you up top all week.
I was. I am not now.
Good. Nobody props the fourth properly.
Mind the ladder. Third rung is a liar.
Best shift I have had in a month.
Sela calls me boy. Everyone does.
That is more like it. Goodnight.
Two suppers today. One at each end.
Cook both and you can be both.
Marrin asked where I learned it.
And you said your mother, and she
smiled, and that was the end of it.
Knowing what a town eats is the work.
The face is only what they look at.
They will want somebody to question.
It should be somebody who can be
frightened well and then let go.
Tell them the truth. The shaft is dry.
That will send them over the water.
Yes. Onto a hole in the ground.
You are Sela, off the fourth level.
She is shaking. Fetch her a blanket.
Nobody here is going to hurt you.

choices.say: You will not let me go.

lines: Dry. You are certain of that.
Thank you. That was kindly done.
Props, to a shaft that gives nothing.
It is dry. Everyone down there knows.
Then it was kind of you to say so.
A quarter of an hour and she gave it up.
People do, when they are frightened.
Tell the muster. We move in the spring.
A true thing, said on purpose.
How did you get in here?
I did not. I am delivering bread.
Nobody marked. Not one of them.
Not a bruise on anybody. Good.
They will think she walked out.
They will think she was let out,
and spend a month arguing about who.
Something in the west field is eating well.
What we bury. Clear it off the strips
before anybody puts a spade in.
No. It has had two hundred years of them.
We feed the field. The field feeds back.
You do not always like what it feeds.
A foot down, along the fence line.
Six spits. Lift the chalk out first.
That is not chalk. That is glass.
It runs the whole length of the fence.
Blackstone dug sixty years for this.
Blackstone dug sixty years towards it.
We have buried rats on top of it since
before either of those walls went up.
One more turn above the ford.
You know what you are standing on now.
Water off the root. Always has been.
That is why nobody else works it,
and why nobody has ever asked why not.
Sit. Sedge on your left, Wick opposite.
Dob has the pot. That is all of us.
Fen is on the water. He gets told after.
Six chairs and a long table. Yes.
Two orders came up this valley arguing.
One took the high ground, one took the
deep ground. Both walked past us.
The kitchen staff stayed where the food
was, which was on top of the seam.
You kept the best of it by standing still.
We kept it by never once mentioning it.
And me. Why send me away at all?
A house that only knows itself is no use.
You were not placed. You were posted.
And you came back knowing both towns
better than either town knows itself.
A bright core and a hollow, one cast.
They are two things. You have two hands.
Neither wall could hold that for a second.
Whitewall would call it bad manners.
Blackstone would call it showing off.
Work. Go and try it on the voles.
Four seasons on the post. Read them back.
Then I will show you what happened
in the fortnight after each one.
Water went up in the spring.
And Blackstone came for the east stands.
Grain went up after the harvest.
And Whitewall marched on the keep.
We set both of those numbers.
We set both of them. On a post,
in chalk, and the rain takes it by winter.
Go on. You have been circling all week.
A boy in the cott row with big hands.
Then a carter out of Blackstone.
Four. Five, if the carter counts twice.
He had two names and both of them worked.
You want me to say which one is real.
Dob is the one who stayed.
That is not the same as real.
It is what I have, and I like it.
Whitewall is on the Drove Road.
Blackstone is coming up from the ford.
On top of it. Of course they will.
One morning, and three ways to spend it.
Say it plainly. I will do the rest.

choices.say: Tend. Show them the root, all of it.
Take. Let them break on the bridge.
Keep. Stop it, and tell nobody.

lines: Both of them went home. That is rare.
The field is a field. Ask me next year.
Straw braid for your belt. It is a long
furrow, and you are on it now.
The chairs want putting away. Go on.
